summary: A creator link page with a till and a list: links and products from one JSON file, click tracking through your own redirect, Stripe Payment Links for anything sold (you never touch card data), and an email capture stored locally. Linktree with two honest bolt-ons.

stack.why: server-rendered page, a redirect, a signup
no cart, no checkout, no card data on your server
the redirect and signup need a process

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your links, bio, avatar and the products you sell
prerequisites.get: Titles, URLs, a one-line bio, a square avatar, and each product's name, price and file.

prerequisites.name: A Stripe account with Payment Links
prerequisites.why: Every product card opens a Payment Link. Enable the send-a-link option so Stripe delivers the file.
prerequisites.get: dashboard.stripe.com > Payment Links > New. Test mode first. Copy each link URL into page.json.

prerequisites.name: A random salt for hashing IPs
prerequisites.why: Click and signup rows store hashes, not addresses.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: The page
phases.goal: Profile, links and products from page.json; JavaScript-free; refuses to boot on a broken file.

steps.detail: profile (name, bio, avatar, accent), links (slug, title, url, emoji, enabled), products (slug, title, price_text, payment_link_url, image).
commands: mkdir creator-page && cd creator-page && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Validate at startup and render server-side, mobile-first

check: A malformed page.json stops the server naming the entry

phases.title: Design
phases.goal: Tap targets, accent, dark mode, focus rings, no external requests.

phases.title: Click tracking
phases.goal: /go/:slug records after redirecting; bots bucketed; /stats private.

steps.do: Implement /go/:slug with the 302 sent before the insert; unknown slugs go home
Bucket bot user agents and build /stats behind basic auth with inline SVG

check: A click lands with one row
The redirect works with the database stopped

phases.title: The store
phases.goal: Product cards open Stripe Payment Links; delivery is Stripe's job.

steps.do: Render product cards linking to payment_link_url
Enable send-a-link delivery on each Payment Link and test a purchase in test mode

check: A test-mode purchase completes and the buyer receives the file link from Stripe

phases.title: Email capture

steps.do: Signup form with honeypot and per-IP rate limit

check: A duplicate email is a no-op
The sixth signup from one IP in an hour is refused
The export opens in a spreadsheet

phases.title: Cards and deploy
phases.goal: OG image, healthz, service, backup, README.

steps.do: OG meta and a generated OG image; /healthz; systemd; Caddy; nightly backup
README: page.json reference, slugs are permanent, Stripe delivery setup

check: The README reaches a live page on your domain

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the page is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A creator page with commerce and a list that you own end to end, with payments handled by Stripe and never by you.

architecture.swap: A small editor writing the file

operations.restore: Deploy from git; copy the database.
operations.incident: A wrong Payment Link is fixed in Stripe and page.json.

notIncluded: Sending email; export into a real sender.
The media kit, brand-deal tooling and the editor.
